title: bug: MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE refuses the wrapper test harnesses when a worker runs them inside its task worktree
description: WT-13's guard (design §6.1) refuses any moe-agent.{sh,ps1} whose path is under <repo>/.worktrees/task-*. A worktree-mode worker that runs `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` or `worktree-landing.sh` from W launches W's own wrapper copy ($ROOT_DIR = W), so every wrapper case prints MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE and fails. Repro: after WT-13 lands, copy scripts/ into <repo>/.worktrees/task-x/ and run its postflight.sh. A harness-only opt-out, or a WT-19 ruling, is needed before wrapper tasks run in worktree mode.

implementationPlan.description:
1. Tests first: wt-guard seam cases and the HEAD repro (RED).

Phase 0:
- Confirm WT-13 landed: `git log -1 --format=%h -E --grep='^(feat|fix)\(task-fbe8e388' HEAD` prints a sha.
- Read its LANDED code at HEAD:
  - moe-agent.sh: `moe_wrapper_in_worktree` and the `if moe_wrapper_in_worktree "$SCRIPT_DIR"; then ... MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE ... exit 1; fi` after it;
  - moe-agent.ps1: `$moeInWorktree = & {...}` and `if ($moeInWorktree) {...}`;
  - postflight-worktree.cjs: `launch()` and `wtGuard` (case 'wt-guard').
- If WT-13 reshaped any of these, apply the same edits to the landed shape. Never change WT-13's detection, message or exit code.
- Re-read this row's comments and #governors first: a later comment can override this plan.

RED repro (the governor's evidence; record it in the step note):
`S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/3c4be125-red.XXXXXX) && git -C "$S" init -q && mkdir -p "$S/.worktrees/task-x" && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C "$S/.worktrees/task-x" && bash "$S/.worktrees/task-x/scripts/tests/postflight.sh"`
It must exit non-zero within seconds and print `[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:`, because its first wrapper launch (the --help check) is refused.

Then edit scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs, with the Edit tool only:
(a) launch(): add `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER:opts.wrapper?null:'1'` to the env object BEFORE `...knobs`.
  - The existing `if(env[k]==null)delete env[k]` loop then drops it for every opts.wrapper copy.
  - So only the suite's own wrapper carries the seam, and a case can still pass it as a knob.
  - The suite's `inherited` scrubs MOE_*, which is why it must be re-added here.
  - Add one comment line saying why, and that copies never get it.
(b) wtGuard: keep the four existing cases and their assertions byte-for-byte. They launch copies, so they now run without the seam and keep proving that a real launch from W is refused. Append two cases:
  - 'wt-guard-optout': the registered-W copy (the same path as 'wt-guard-in') with knob {MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER:'1'} must give code 0, cliRan, and no MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE in the log.
  - 'wt-guard-optout-strict': the same copy with each of 'true', ' 1' and '0' must give code 1, the `[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:` line, no CLI and no .moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl.
  - Put the value in each assertion message, and update the wtGuard header comment.

Fast RED, in a scratch scripts snapshot, never the shared tree (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-mutant-copy):
`T=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/3c4be125-wt.XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C "$T" && cp scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs "$T/scripts/tests/" && mkdir "$T/tmp" && cp scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$T/tmp/fake-proxy.js" && env $(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-guard node "$T/scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs" sh "$T/scripts/moe-agent.sh" "$T/tmp/fake-proxy.js" "$T/tmp" "$(command -v bash)"`
Expected RED: an AssertionError at wt-guard-optout, because the wrapper still refuses. A TypeError or other harness fault is not RED.

error handling: every new test assertion names its case and value; no other case changes.

2. The wrapper twins honour the exact-'1' seam (Edit tool only).

scripts/moe-agent.sh:
- Change only the refusal condition, to `if [ "${MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER:-}" != 1 ] && moe_wrapper_in_worktree "$SCRIPT_DIR"; then`.
- Keep the function, the message and `exit 1`.
- Add a short comment covering:
  - it is a test seam only, set by the launcher harnesses (postflight.{sh,ps1}, postflight-worktree.cjs, worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}) so a worktree-mode worker can run them from its own W (task-3c4be125);
  - exactly '1' skips this one refusal, and nothing else reads it;
  - no launch path sets it: not the IDE plugins, moe-team, operators or runbooks.
- The Edit tool is rename-safe for running seats and leaves the TOOL witness these contested paths need (mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse).
- Then run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Keep bash 3.2 syntax.

scripts/moe-agent.ps1:
- `if ($moeInWorktree -and $env:MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER -cne '1') {`, with the twin comment.
- -cne is case-sensitive, so $null, 'true', ' 1' and '0' all keep the refusal.
- Keep the UTF-8 BOM and LF endings. The file must still parse on PS 5.1.

error handling:
- This is a pure string compare on an env value, with no new IO or git call.
- Unset, or any other value, takes WT-13's refusal path and exit 1 unchanged.
- A failed git probe stays fail-open, exactly as WT-13 landed it.
- The name sits outside the MOE_WORKTREE_/LAND_/CONTROL_/BOARD_/COMMIT_/ATTR_ code families and does not contain the substring MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE, so the code-family greps and wt-guard's log asserts are unaffected (mem:gotcha-wrapper-code-family-grep-counts-identifiers).

GREEN:
- Rerun step 1's fast test command with both twins also copied into $T/scripts/: wt-guard passes on sh.
- Then run PS 5.1 from WSL on the same $T. It must pass (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-mutant-copy):
`cd "$T" && MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-guard WSLENV=MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" "$(wslpath -w "$T/scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs")" ps1 "$(wslpath -w "$T/scripts/moe-agent.ps1")" "$(wslpath -w "$T/tmp/fake-proxy.js")" "$(wslpath -w "$T/tmp")" powershell`

3. The harnesses set the seam. Edit tool only, and no case, assertion or expected-list changes.

scripts/tests/postflight.sh:
- Add `export MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER=1` directly after `export MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off`.
- Add a two-line comment: a worktree-mode worker runs this harness from its own task worktree, where WT-13's guard refuses the wrapper copy; postflight-worktree.cjs re-adds the seam for its own wrapper only, so its refusal cases stay real.
- This covers:
  - every direct "$WRAPPER" launch;
  - postflight-owner-guard.cjs, which inherits MOE_* (it filters only FAKE_/OG_);
  - the frozen suite, which inherits everything except GIT_/HOME/TMP.

scripts/tests/postflight.ps1:
- Add `$env:MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER = '1'` directly after `$env:MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION = 'off'`, with the twin comment.
- Keep its BOM.

scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh:
- Inside the WTJS suite's launch, add `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER:'1'` to the `env` object right after `MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION:'off'`, with a one-line comment.
- The suite's `inherited` scrubs MOE_*, so this is the only place the seam can enter.
- worktree-landing.ps1 extracts this same suite between the WTJS markers, so it needs no edit.
- The held-out cases, the `--list` output and worktree-landing.ps1's $expectedCases stay unchanged; that key and its comment are the whole diff.

Out of scope: do NOT touch the other launcher suites (agent-git-guard, protected-agent-command, agent-runtime, wave1-pilot, mention-provenance, worktree-e2e). They are filed as a follow-up row.

error handling:
- None of these lines adds IO.
- A missing or misspelled key shows up only as the refusal when run from W, which step 4's test commands catch.
- Run `bash -n` on both .sh harnesses after editing.

4. Verification: run once, fresh, from task-worktree copies.

Before running:
- `git status --short scripts/` must list only this task's six files. Otherwise peers' bytes would enter the overlay: attribute them and wait (mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint).

How to run:
- Run both legs from the repo root /mnt/d/projexts/moes.
- Each leg takes longer than the Bash tool's 10-minute cap, so write each exact command into its own scratch script under /mnt/d/moe-scratch.
- Start each with `( set -m; nohup bash <script> > <log> 2>&1 < /dev/null & echo $! > <pidfile> )`. `set -m` keeps SIGINT un-ignored, which postflight scenario W needs.
- Wait with bounded `timeout 590` polls.
- Run the two legs concurrently, and kill only recorded PIDs (mem:gotcha-qa-windows-launcher-tests-from-wsl, mem:gotcha-harness-snapshot-needs-full-archive).

BASH LEG (this is the complete_task verification), verbatim:
U=$(env|awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ",$1}') && B=$(git log -1 --format=%H -E --grep='^(feat|fix)\(task-fbe8e388' HEAD) && S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/3c4be125.XXXXXX) && git -C "$S" init -q && H="$S/.worktrees/task-head" && W="$S/.worktrees/task-x" && mkdir -p "$H" "$W" && git archive "$B" scripts|tar -x -C "$H" && git archive HEAD scripts|tar -x -C "$W" && cp --parents scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} scripts/tests/{postflight.{sh,ps1},postflight-worktree.cjs,worktree-landing.sh} "$W" && ! env $U bash "$H/scripts/tests/postflight.sh" >"$S/h.log" 2>&1 && grep -qF '[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:' "$S/h.log" && { env $U MOE_PROXY_PATH=/none bash "$W/scripts/moe-agent.sh" --project "$S" --role worker --no-start-daemon --no-loop >"$S/s.log" 2>&1; test $? -eq 1; } && grep -qF '[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:' "$S/s.log" && env $U node "$W/scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs" bash && env $U bash "$W/scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh" && bash "$W/scripts/tests/parity-check.sh"

What the bash leg proves:
- the governor's repro fails on WT-13's landed completion bytes (task-head, $B);
- a seat-shaped launch of the W copy without the seam exits 1 with the refusal line. MOE_PROXY_PATH=/none and --no-start-daemon mean nothing could reach a daemon even if the guard failed open;
- from the W copy, postflight-safe prints failureClass NONE. That covers every postflight.sh case, both node suites and the new wt-guard cases;
- worktree-landing.sh passes all cases, and parity-check passes.
Expect exit 0.

PS 5.1 LEG, verbatim:
P=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/3c4be125-ps.XXXXXX) && git -C "$P" init -q && W="$P/.worktrees/task-x" && mkdir -p "$W" && git archive HEAD scripts|tar -x -C "$W" && cp --parents scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} scripts/tests/{postflight.{sh,ps1},postflight-worktree.cjs,worktree-landing.sh} "$W" && cd "$W" && { powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File 'scripts\moe-agent.ps1' -Project "$(wslpath -w "$P")" -WorkerId worker-x -Role worker -NoStartDaemon -NoLoop >"$P/s.log" 2>&1; test $? -eq 1; } && grep -qF '[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:' "$P/s.log" && "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell && powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File 'scripts\tests\worktree-landing.ps1'

Expect exit 0: the ps1 seat probe is refused, postflight-safe powershell prints NONE, and worktree-landing.ps1 exits 0.
- Windows git accepts a WSL-created D: scratch repo (probed 2026-11-02).
- pwsh 7 is optional (`... postflight-safe.mjs pwsh`); CI runs it.
- On a native Windows seat, build the same `git init` + .worktrees\task-x copy in PowerShell and run the same three checks.

On any failure:
- Re-run that harness raw from the same copy (postflight-safe hides output).
- Fix only within the six files, then run BOTH legs fresh again.
- Save each leg's command, exit code and output tail.

5. Adversarial self-review, then complete_task. Load adversarial-self-review, then check:

(1) Only the refusal condition reads the seam. WT-13's detection, message and exit are byte-identical: `git diff` shows only the condition and comments.

(2) `git grep -n MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER` lists only the six files: never moe-team.*, moe-jetbrains/**, moe-vscode/**, packages/** or docs/**. This is the evidence that real launch paths never set it.

(3) Mutants. Run one at a time in scratch copies, never the shared tree, and restore each afterwards (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-mutant-copy):
- M1: sh condition reverted to `if moe_wrapper_in_worktree "$SCRIPT_DIR"; then` → wt-guard fails at wt-guard-optout.
- M2: sh test changed to `[ -z "${MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER:-}" ]` → wt-guard fails at wt-guard-optout-strict ('true').
- M3: ps1 `-and ... -cne '1'` removed → wt-guard fails under PS 5.1.
- M4: postflight.sh export deleted in a W copy → that copy's postflight.sh fails at its first launch with MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE.
- M5: launch()'s default key deleted in a W copy → `MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-board` from that copy fails with the refusal.
Each kill must be the named AssertionError or refusal line, never a harness fault.

(4) Concurrency and state: the seam is a read-only env lookup, with no files and no locks, so concurrent seats or harnesses cannot race on it. A real seat's env never has it, and WSL interop does not forward it to Windows processes (each harness sets it per engine).

(5) Size: `git diff --numstat` on the six files should show under 60 net lines.

Then:
- If any bytes change, re-run both legs.
- Call complete_task with the bash-leg verification (command, exitCode, outputTail).
- Report modifiedFiles as exactly the six files.
- The summary must carry: the RED repro; the PS-leg command, exit code and JSON line; and the mutant kills.

This step adds no error handling of its own: any test failure loops back to step 4.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: one env test seam, MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER, honoured only when it is exactly '1'. This follows the governor's 15:16Z constraint comment-9328a06f: an env var that the harnesses set and real launch paths never set, not a blanket bypass.

Rejected:
(1) Scoping the guard to launches whose --project is in the wrapper's own repository. It needs no harness edits, but a real seat launched from W against another project would start. That breaks the governor's constraint and WT-13's documented §6.1 rule.
(2) A seam whose value names the allowed W path. It needs path canonicalization across WSL, MSYS and Windows, for no gain: the threat is the worker's own W anyway.
(3) The caller setting the var on the verification command line. The cjs suites scrub MOE_*, and WT-14's gate scrubs MOE_* before starting the harness, so the harness itself has to set it.
(4) A non-MOE_ name that slips through the suites' env filters. That is hidden coupling to the filter regexes, and wt-guard's refusal cases would inherit it too.
(5) A notice line whenever the seam is used. Harness output would then depend on where it runs, and in-place and from-W runs could diverge.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
How each harness passes env to the wrapper:
- postflight.sh's direct "$WRAPPER" launches inherit the harness env. postflight.sh already sets MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off at its top, and postflight.ps1 has the twin line.
- postflight.sh/ps1 run three node suites:
  - the frozen suite inherits everything except GIT_/HOME/TMP;
  - postflight-owner-guard.cjs inherits MOE_*, filtering only FAKE_/OG_;
  - postflight-worktree.cjs scrubs MOE_* and builds each launch env as {...inherited, ..., ...knobs}, then deletes null values. That makes a per-copy default a one-liner, and only launch() spawns the full wrapper there; the other engine spawns extract functions.
- worktree-landing.sh's WTJS suite scrubs MOE_|CLAUDE|GIT_|FAKE_. worktree-landing.ps1 extracts that same suite, so one key covers both engines.

Other facts:
- parity-check only greps the wrappers, so it already runs from W.
- postflight.sh references ROOT_DIR only for scripts/. postflight-safe, worktree-landing and parity-check need only a scripts/ copy.
- Windows git accepts a git-init'ed scratch repo created from WSL on D: (probed 2026-11-02: show-prefix `.worktrees/task-x/scripts/`).
- Both leg commands were syntax-checked with bash -n. cp --parents with nested braces copies exactly the six files, and the `^(feat|fix)\(task-<id8>` grep finds WT-12's completion 1f9950ee.
